title: Customer initials
prompt: Name badges show each customer's initials. Write `solve(customers)` so it returns `customer_id` and `initials`: the first letter of each word of `name`, in capitals. A UDF is a fine way to do it.
rules: Words are separated by one or more spaces; spaces at the start or end don't count.
Initials are in capitals: `ana ruiz` gives `AR`. A name made only of spaces gives an empty string.
A missing name gives a missing `initials`.
Return `customer_id` and `initials`, both text, in that order. Keep every customer.
hints: In Python, `name.split()` with no argument splits on any run of spaces and ignores spaces at the ends.
Return `None` when the name is `None`, so a missing name doesn't stop the job.
Wrap the function with `F.udf(function, "string")`, or use the `@F.udf("string")` decorator.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(customers):
    # Return customer_id and the initials of each name.
    return customers
